season.evidence: Web search: a guide service says early July through end of August for Vesper alpine climbs; Mountaineers late-July reports; True Grit's own logged ascents fall in Jul (3), Aug (4), Sep (6), Oct (1).

track.why: Logged route is True Grit and the report places the party at the true base after an off-route detour, describes the bolted pitches and the pitch-4 crux; the track runs trailhead to summit and back with the stash at the col notch. Round trip within 40 m of our trailhead pin, summit within 5 m.

otherTracksConsidered.why: Also logged True Grit in September, complete round trip, but no report text to confirm the line; kept as a backup only.

facts.text: A grassy ramp just left of the real start tempts parties off route; it has loose holds and is serious to reverse (August)

The two usual ways to the col notch near 5,720 ft are a traverse north from the trail at about 5,630 ft or a line hugging the west side of Lake Elan; going higher than that forces a slick slab down-climb to reach the col (August).
Packs are commonly left at the notch near 5,720 ft; the base of the first pitch is a short scramble further along the ledge.
Pitch 4 is the standout crux and feels harder than the grade; the bolts and belay stations are plentiful and in good shape.
The ledge traverse below the col is narrow with no-fall consequences, though the dirt underfoot is firm (August)
In mid-August there was no snow on the approach and no stream crossing that needed wading.
Trekking poles for the long knee-punishing descent (August)

notes: Only two of the peak's routes were in scope. Fish & Whistle has no harvested track (one September logged ascent exists on Peakbagger but no track was in the packet). Ragged Edge already has track points. North Face (wa_vesper_peak_north_face) and the standard route were not in routes[].
